did.abstract: Harvey Sacks (d.1975) taught in the Department of Sociology at UC Irvine, UC Berkeley and UC Los Angeles (ca. 1960s-72). He is best known for his work in ethnomethodology and conversational analysis. The collection consists of notes, drafts, diaries, unpublished lectures, tapes, lectures, and miscellaneous materials related to Sacks' life and work.

Library Special Collections provides a standard level of preservation and access for all collections and, when time and resources permit, conducts more intensive processing. We are committed to providing ethical, inclusive, and anti-racist description of the materials we steward, and to remediating existing description of our materials that contains language that may be offensive or cause harm. bioghist.head: Biography
bioghist.p: Sacks worked for the University of California, ca. 1960s-72; he taught in the Department of Sociology at UC Irvine, at UC Berkeley and UC Los Angeles; best known for his work in ethnomethodology and conversational analysis; died in 1975 when he was 40 years old.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Content
scopecontent.p: Collection consists of notes, drafts, diaries, unpublished lectures, tapes, lectures, and miscellaneous materials related to the life and work of Harvey Sacks.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Boxes 15-17 contain work tapes. Box 17 also contains the Ann Arbor Lectures transcripts, as well as the transcript of work tape 10.
